Product Overview

Pet Robot is a desktop electronic pet based on the ESP32-C3 microcontroller. It displays a pair of lively animated eyes on an SSD1306 OLED screen, coupled with an MPU6050 six-axis gyroscope for motion sensing, and can produce 23 expressions and 19 daily activity animations, making it an entertaining and low-power desktop companion.

23 Dynamic Expressions

Happy, Surprised, Confused, Sleepy, Angry, Pain, Dizzy, Curious, Looking Around, and more. Each expression has its own dynamic behavior animation and duration.

19 Daily Activities

Drinking, Reading, Eating, Dancing, Drawing, Gaming, Eating Ice Cream, Taking Photos, Writing, Exercising, Brushing Teeth, Cooking, Bathing, Making Phone Calls, Eating Noodles, Looking in Mirror, Stretching, and more.

RTC Timekeeping

After a single WiFi NTP sync, WiFi is disconnected while the internal RTC keeps time continuously, even after power loss (not lost during deep sleep), with automatic daily midnight calibration.

Smart Power Saving

Automatic screen brightness adjustment, dynamic CPU frequency scaling, WiFi disconnects when not in use, auto deep sleep when idle — designed for battery-powered compact spaces.

Motion Sensing

Step counter, single/double tap detection, tilt detection, drop/shake/flick motion recognition. Each motion triggers a different pet reaction.

Mood System

100-point mood value, decays 5 points every 60 seconds without interaction, +10 per interaction, +15 per double tap, -10 per flick. Mood influences expression tendencies.

Wiring Guide

I2C Shared Bus SSD1306 and MPU6050 share the same I2C bus (GPIO3=SDA, GPIO4=SCL). The two devices have different I2C addresses (0x3C and 0x68), so there is no conflict.

Wiring Table

ESP32-C3SSD1306 OLEDMPU6050Description
3.3VVCCVCCPower positive
GNDGNDGNDPower negative
GPIO3SDASDAI2C Data Line
GPIO4SCLSCLI2C Clock Line

Wiring Diagram


    ESP32-C3              SSD1306 OLED          MPU6050
    ┌─────────┐           ┌──────────┐          ┌──────────┐
    │  3.3V   ├───────────┤   VCC    │──────────┤   VCC    │
    │   GND   ├───────────┤   GND    │──────────┤   GND    │
    │  GPIO3  ├───────────┤   SDA    │──────────┤   SDA    │
    │  GPIO4  ├───────────┤   SCL    │──────────┤   SCL    │
    │  GPIO9  │(onboard)  │          │          │          │
    └─────────┘           └──────────┘          └──────────┘
Wiring Precautions
  • Some SSD1306 modules may have an I2C address of 0x3D. If the display is abnormal, check the resistor soldering on the back of the module.
  • When the MPU6050 AD0 pin is connected to GND, the address is 0x68; when connected to 3.3V, the address is 0x69. The code defaults to 0x68.
  • It is recommended to use 4.7kΩ pull-up resistors on SDA/SCL to 3.3V (most modules already have these built in).

First Power-On vs Deep Sleep Wakeup On first power-on (reconnecting power), RTC starts from 0:00 and will attempt WiFi search for 60 seconds. When waking from deep sleep, RTC maintains the previous time and skips WiFi to run directly.

WiFi & Time Sync

Time Sync Strategy

Pet Robot uses an RTC-first power-saving time strategy, with WiFi connecting only briefly when necessary:

ScenarioBehaviorWiFi Search Duration
First power-on (RTC = 0:00)Search saved WiFi → NTP sync → Disconnect WiFi60 seconds
Deep sleep wakeupSkip WiFi, RTC maintains time0 seconds
Daily midnight (00:00~00:05)Connect WiFi to calibrate time, once daily60 seconds
Triple-click to enter AP modeStart AP hotspot + Web config interfaceUntil user action

→ Disconnect WiFi immediately

3b

RTC continues
Start from 0:00

When No Saved WiFi If never configured (no saved WiFi credentials), the device will not search for WiFi on power-on and will run directly with RTC starting from 0:00. After entering AP mode via triple-click to configure the network, credentials will be saved for subsequent automatic connection.

NTP Server

Default uses pool.ntp.org, timezone is UTC+8 (Beijing time). NTP sync timeout is 15 seconds.

ParameterOptionsDescription
Screen Refresh Rate10 / 20 / 30 / 40 / 50 FPSDefault 30 FPS. Lower = more power saving, Higher = smoother
Gyroscope Sample Rate10 / 20 / 50 / 100 HzDefault 50 Hz. Lower = more power saving, slower response
Motion Cooldown0.5s / 1s / 2s / 3sDefault 1s. Minimum interval between motion events

Auto DimOn / OffDefault on. Lower screen brightness when idle
Power Saving ModeOn / OffDefault off. When enabled, CPU downclocks to 80 MHz, forces low brightness
Power Saving Tips The configuration interface displays a tip: "Lower frequency = more power saving". RTC continues running after shutdown. All settings are saved in Flash and are not lost on power-off.

Power Management

Multi-Layer Power Saving Strategy

LayerTrigger ConditionMeasure
WiFi DisconnectAfter NTP sync completesImmediately turn off WiFi module
Screen Slightly DimNo interaction 10sBrightness reduced to 80/255
Screen Very DimNo interaction 20sBrightness reduced to 20/255
Power Saving ModeManually enabled by userCPU 80 MHz + forced dim brightness
DrowsyIdle timeout reached5s eye-closing animation → Enter sleep
SleepDrowsy animation endsEyes closed, brightness stays at DIM level
Deep SleepLong press button 3sESP32 deep sleep, RTC active, BOOT button wakeup

Deep Sleep

Long press the BOOT button for 3 seconds to enter deep sleep. At this point:

  • ESP32-C3 enters deep sleep state, power consumption drops to ~5 µA
  • Internal RTC continues running, time is not lost
  • Press BOOT button to wake up, shows Surprised expression then returns to normal
  • After wakeup, skips the 15-second boot phase and directly enters normal interaction
Battery Power Recommendations Due to limited space, a 200-400 mAh small lithium battery is recommended. Under power saving mode + 30 FPS configuration, expected battery life is approximately 8-12 hours. In deep sleep mode, it can standby for several days.

State Machine

Pet behavior is driven by the following state machine:

  • Default — Default state, randomly switches expressions or activities when idle
  • Boot Phase — First 15 seconds, only switches between Surprised and Stretching
  • Normal Phase — Looking Around 60%, other 10 expressions 4% each
  • Interaction Triggered — Button/Tap/Tilt/Motion → Corresponding expression
  • Idle Timeout — Reaches idleTimeout → Drowsy → Sleep
  • Sleep Wakeup — Any interaction → Surprised expression → Normal state

Troubleshooting

ProblemPossible CauseSolution
Screen not displaying I2C address error or loose wiring Check wiring, verify I2C address is 0x3C (not 0x3D)
Screen shows "No I2C devices found" I2C bus not connected Check SDA/SCL wiring, verify power supply is normal
MPU6050 not detected AD0 pin level incorrect AD0 to GND → address 0x68; AD0 to 3.3V → address 0x69
Time not displayed (--:--) RTC not synced Triple-click to enter AP mode, connect WiFi to complete NTP sync
WiFi connection failed Wrong password or weak signal Re-enter AP mode, select the correct WiFi and enter password
Expression not switching Insufficient idle time Requires 6+ seconds of idle time before switching expressions
Pet always sleeping Idle timeout set too short Enter AP mode, increase idle timeout (e.g., 120s)
Tap not responding Tap force insufficient Requires acceleration > 15 m/s², gently tap the desk
Button not responding GPIO pin conflict Verify using GPIO9 (BOOT button)
Deep sleep cannot wake up Wakeup source not configured Press BOOT button to wake (GPIO9 active low)
Compilation error Missing dependencies Run pio lib install to install all dependencies

Serial Debugging

Connect ESP32-C3 via USB and use the serial monitor (115200 bps) to view runtime logs:

pio device monitor --baud 115200

The log will display detailed information such as I2C scan results, RTC status, WiFi connection process, and motion detection results.

Build & Flash 
# Build
pio run

# Build and flash
pio run --target upload

# View serial output
pio device monitor --baud 115200
